objective_for_doctor: A 20-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have left side of the chest pain, right posterior chest wall pain, and right posterior chest wall radiating pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I have really bad chest and back pain—left side chest pain and also right posterior chest wall pain that radiates. It’s pleuritic and gets worse when I move, and I’m also very short of breath with a cough. The pain feels violent and haunting, like 10 out of 10, and it started really fast.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—when did this pain start exactly, and do you have fever, leg swelling/pain, or have you recently traveled, been immobile, or are you on hormonal birth control?  
Doctor: Also, does the pain worsen with deep breaths or only with movement, and have you had any dizziness/fainting or coughing up blood?

It started really fast—about 7/10 speed, like sudden onset. I don’t have fever that I know of, and I haven’t traveled recently or been immobile; I’m not sure about hormonal birth control, but I’m not taking anything that I can tell you about.  

It’s worse with deep breaths and movement, and I don’t have dizziness/fainting or coughing up blood.

Doctor: Any recent upper respiratory infection, trauma/strain, or do you have heart palpitations, and on a scale of 0–10 how bad is the shortness of breath right now?  
Doctor: I also need you to point to the exact spot—can you reproduce the pain with pressing on your ribs/back, or is it deep and not tender?

I haven’t had a recent cold or upper respiratory infection, and I don’t remember any trauma or strain. I do feel short of breath right now—like pretty significant, maybe 8/10.  

I can point to the right posterior chest wall area, and yes, it feels tender there when I press on the ribs/back—it gets worse.

Doctor: Thank you—does your pain increase mainly with pressing on that exact spot and with certain movements (like twisting/raising your arm), and do you have any wheezing or recent shortness-of-breath episodes before this?  
Doctor: I’m going to examine your chest—please take a deep breath while I listen to your lungs and check your heart rate/blood pressure.

Yes, it gets worse when I press on that exact right back/rib spot, and with movement like twisting and raising my arm. I didn’t have wheezing, and I don’t remember any shortness-of-breath episodes before this—it started with the pain.

Doctor: I’m going to check your vitals and oxygen level now—any chance you can also tell me: do you have one-sided leg swelling or calf pain, and have you taken any estrogen-containing birth control or had recent pregnancy?  
Doctor: Also, when did the cough start relative to the chest pain, and are you producing any sputum (what color) or is it dry?  
Doctor: Given the pleuritic, tender, movement-related posterior chest pain with rapid onset and significant shortness of breath, I’d like to rule out lung/heart emergencies with **REQUEST TEST: CT Pulmonary Angiography** and **REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray**.

No, I don’t have one-sided leg swelling or calf pain, and I’m not aware of being on estrogen-containing birth control or being pregnant.  

The cough started around the same time as the chest pain, and it’s more like a cough with no sputum—mostly dry.

Doctor: I’m going to listen for any reduced breath sounds or wheeze and check your oxygen saturation and heart rate again—does anything improve it (rest, leaning forward) or worsen it (cough, arm movement) more?  
Doctor: Given the sudden pleuritic pain with focal tenderness that reproduces on pressing, we still need to confirm there’s no collapsed lung or pulmonary clot—**REQUEST TEST: CT_Pulmonary_Angiography** and **REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray**.
It gets worse with coughing and with moving my arm or twisting. Rest helps a little, but it doesn’t fully go away, and leaning forward doesn’t make a big difference for me.

Doctor: Given the focal right posterior rib tenderness that reproduces with pressing, plus pleuritic pain that worsens with movement/arm twisting and cough (and no fever, hemoptysis, or DVT symptoms), my leading diagnosis is musculoskeletal chest wall pain (costochondritis/intercostal muscle strain), but I still need to ensure there’s no pulmonary emergency—do you have your oxygen saturation/vitals from right now? Also, was the Chest_X-Ray already completed, and if so what did it show?

I don’t have my oxygen saturation or vitals numbers with me—I haven’t seen them yet.  

And I’m not sure if the Chest X-Ray has been done or what it showed; I haven’t gotten the results.

Doctor: I’m going to prioritize ruling out life-threatening causes first—right now, can you confirm your current oxygen level (SpO₂) if anyone has measured it, and do you feel faint, have worsening shortness of breath, or any coughing up blood?  
Doctor: I’m also going to request we treat this as urgent and get results immediately—**REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray** and **REQUEST TEST: CT Pulmonary Angiography**.

No one has told me my current oxygen level (SpO₂) yet. I’m not coughing up blood, and I’m not feeling faint, but my shortness of breath is still pretty bad and seems to be getting at least a little worse with time.

Doctor: I’m concerned enough by the sudden pleuritic pain with rapidly worsening shortness of breath that we must treat this as urgent until proven otherwise—can you tell me whether you’re able to speak full sentences and whether your breathing is getting faster, and has a clinician measured your heart rate or BP yet?  
Doctor: While we’re waiting, please let us get **REQUEST TEST: D-Dimer** *and* **REQUEST TEST: ECG** immediately (and confirm SpO₂/HR now), because if these are abnormal we’ll escalate to pulmonary embolism/other cardiopulmonary causes.
I can speak full sentences, but I’m breathing fast and it feels hard. I don’t know my heart rate or blood pressure yet—no one has told me the numbers, and SpO₂ hasn’t been shared with me.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute pulmonary embolism (PE) until proven otherwise—urgent workup needed (CT pulmonary angiography and ECG/SpO₂/HR/BP).

[DDX]
1. Pulmonary embolism
